subject: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@bridgewalk.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@bridgewalk.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18 15:02 PDT
Subject: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Attached is a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) I drafted to align on the POC environment setup and a proposed three-week cadence so we can get a validated evaluation window quickly. High-level asks to unblock us:

- Org + account: please confirm the BridgeWalk org name (GCP project or Azure subscription) you want us to provision evaluation artifacts under.
- API access: do you prefer long-lived service account keys or short-lived API keys for the hosted evaluation? We support both but need the approach to be decided before week-1 tasks.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide a small list of Redwood egress addresses to allow. If you'd rather keep traffic private, we can peer VPCs instead (see below).
- VPC peering: if you choose peering, please share the VPC CIDR(s) and your infra contact so we can coordinate routes and firewall rules.

Proposed milestone summary (also in the attached MAP):
- Week 0 (this week): agree on org, API key approach, infra contacts, and sign MAP.
- Week 1: create BridgeWalk evaluation org entry, provision API keys/service account, exchange egress IPs or initiate peering request.
- Week 2: complete IP allowlist or finish peering, run smoke tests, validate connectivity.
- Week 3: run sample inference load, collect perf metrics, roll to sample users for feature validation.

Can you confirm the cloud provider (GCP/Azure/AWS), relevant VPC CIDR, and the owner for infrastructure (email) so we can draft the peering request? I attached the MAP draft and a simple network diagram that shows both options (egress allowlist vs VPC peering).

Best,
Jonas Weber
Technical Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

---

From: Elena Park <elena@bridgewalk.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@bridgewalk.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18 17:24 PDT
Subject: Re: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick answers:

- Cloud: GCP (project: bridgewalk-eval-2026).
- VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (we have a peering-only subgroup we prefer to use).
- Infra contact: infrastructure@bridgewalk.ai (cc'd on this thread).
- API access: security wants short-lived credentials if possible; they asked whether a service account with workload identity is an option instead of static API keys.

Concern: our security ops team prefers peering over public egress allowlisting where feasible. If peering requires extra approvals and will delay the POC by more than a week, we can temporarily open an allowlist for the Redwood egress IPs during the evaluation window.

I'll review the MAP with Tom and get back with signoff by Monday. Also, can you confirm the minimum set of firewall ports needed?

Cheers,
Elena Park
Head of Platform
BridgeWalk

---

On Sat, Sep 19, 2026 at 09:08, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@bridgewalk.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@bridgewalk.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19 09:08 PDT
Subject: Re: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan

Thanks, Elena — that all sounds reasonable. Short answers inline and an ask for next steps: 

- Short-lived credentials: yes — we can issue short-lived API tokens via a secure link for the hosted evaluation; alternatively, a GCP Service Account + Workload Identity is fully supported if you want fully private auth. For the quickest path, the short-lived token route is usually the fastest.
- Peering vs allowlist: peering is our preferred pattern for private production traffic but for POCs we often do a hybrid: initiate peering (it can be completed in parallel) and temporarily allowlist our egress addresses to avoid a hard blocker. I'll attach our current egress CSV for your security team to review.
- Firewall ports: primarily HTTPS (443) outbound to our egress addresses; if you plan to do deeper health checks we may ask for inbound from a small set of IPs (we'll call that out if needed).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether you'd like short-lived tokens or SA with workload identity (reply here).
2) Infra team to open a peering ticket with the VPC CIDR above and list 'infrastructure@bridgewalk.ai' as owner.
3) If temporary allowlist is desired, let us know and we'll provide the final egress list and date range.

Attaching MAP v1 (updated with the short-lived token option) and the egress IP CSV. Happy to jump on a 30-minute network walkthrough next week.

-j

---

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@bridgewalk.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21 11:42 PDT
Subject: Re: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan

Hi Elena / infra team —

I'm Priyom, tech lead on Redwood's private connectivity and onboarding. A few implementation notes to make the peering path smooth:

- Peering checklist (high level):
  - Share VPC CIDR (you've shared 10.40.0.0/16) and confirm there are no overlapping ranges.
  - Confirm project ID: bridgewalk-eval-2026.
  - Provide a dedicated peering route (we recommend a /20 allocation for test subnets).
  - Confirm which services will need SNAT exemption (if any).

- IAM roles: we'll need an infra contact that can create/accept the VPC peering and update routes (roles: compute.networkAdmin or equivalent).

- Sample routes / NAT: if you are using Private Google Access, ensure the routes allow traffic to our peering ranges; otherwise temporary egress allowlist will require an ACL entry for 443.

- Troubleshooting items: please keep Cloud VPN and Cloud NAT settings visible to the team for the initial health checks.

If helpful, here's a short internal playbook link and a Terraform snippet we often share for peering: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-BridgeWalk-MAP (peering playbook).

I'm available Tue/Wed next week 10:00-13:00 PT for a 30-minute network walkthrough. Can Elena or the infra team confirm a slot?

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

---

From: Elena Park <elena@bridgewalk.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-23 09:45 PDT
Subject: Re: BridgeWalk POC: access & network milestone plan

Thanks, Priyom and Jonas —

We reviewed the MAP with our security and infra teams and agreed to move forward with the peering-first approach; infra will open the peering ticket today and look to complete it by next Thursday (2026-09-30). For speed, we'll also allowlist Redwood egress for the week of 2026-09-27 to avoid any blocker to beginning smoke tests.

Available for the network walkthrough: Tue 2026-09-28 10:30 PT. Please send a calendar invite. Also, please push the MAP to DocuSign when you have the final edits and we'll sign on behalf of BridgeWalk.

Elena
Head of Platform, BridgeWalk
elena@bridgewalk.ai
